afrobeats.description: A genre originating in West Africa — particularly Nigeria and Ghana — blending West African rhythms with Western pop, hip-hop, and R&B. Characterized by infectious polyrhythmic percussion, melodic hooks, and artists like Burna Boy, Wizkid, and Davido.

pop.description: Popular music characterized by catchy melodies, verse-chorus structure, and broad mainstream appeal. Typically features polished production, accessible lyrics, and danceable rhythms.

rock.description: Guitar-driven music built around electric guitars, bass, and drums. Ranges from classic rock to hard rock, with emphasis on rhythm, power chords, and vocal energy.

hip-hop.description: A genre built around rhythmic vocal delivery over sampled or produced beats. Originated in 1970s New York and has grown into one of the world's most dominant genres across trap, conscious rap, and drill.

jazz.description: An improvisational genre rooted in African American musical traditions, characterized by complex harmonies, syncopated rhythms, and expressive instrumentation. Ranges from upbeat swing to contemplative cool jazz and late-night bossa nova.

electronic.description: Music produced primarily with electronic instruments and digital audio workstations. Encompasses a wide range of styles from ambient textures to high-energy club music, united by synthesized sound design.

indie.description: Independent music characterized by DIY production aesthetics and artistic freedom outside the mainstream. Indie spans many styles but prioritizes authentic expression, introspective lyrics, and unconventional song structures.

r&b.description: Rhythm and Blues combines soulful vocals with groovy rhythms and smooth production. Modern R&B blends hip-hop, pop, and soul into melodic tracks centered on love, relationships, and emotional expression.

soul.description: An emotionally expressive genre rooted in gospel and R&B, soul music emphasizes powerful vocals, heartfelt lyrics, and rich orchestral arrangements. Artists like Aretha Franklin and Marvin Gaye defined its emotional depth.

funk.description: A highly rhythmic genre built around syncopated bass lines, percussive guitar riffs, and tight horn sections. Funk prioritizes the groove above everything else — if it makes you move, it's working.

reggae.description: Originating in Jamaica in the late 1960s, reggae is defined by its syncopated rhythm guitar skank, heavy bass lines, and socially conscious or spiritual lyrics. Bob Marley remains its most internationally recognized ambassador.

country.description: American roots music blending folk, blues, and Western traditions with storytelling lyrics and acoustic instrumentation including guitar, fiddle, and pedal steel. Themes range from rural life and heartbreak to resilience and celebration.

classical.description: Western art music spanning orchestral, chamber, and solo instrumental traditions. Known for complexity, formal structure, and profound emotional range — from the delicate counterpoint of Bach to the sweeping romanticism of Tchaikovsky.

lofi.description: Lo-fi hip hop features intentionally low-fidelity audio — vinyl crackle, dusty samples, muffled beats — layered over slow mellow hip-hop rhythms. It became the defining study and focus genre of the 2010s streaming era.

ambient.description: Atmospheric music designed to evoke environment and mood rather than demand attention. Pioneered by Brian Eno, ambient music uses texture, tone, and slow evolution to create immersive soundscapes that blur the line between music and atmosphere.

folk.description: Acoustic music rooted in oral traditions and regional storytelling, blending fingerpicked guitar, honest lyrics, and natural recording aesthetics. Contemporary folk artists like Fleet Foxes and Iron & Wine have brought the genre to new audiences.

blues.description: Expressive guitar-based music originating in African American culture of the Deep South. Blues is characterized by the blues scale, call-and-response phrasing, bending notes, and themes of perseverance through hardship.

metal.description: A high-intensity genre built around heavily distorted guitars, aggressive or operatic vocals, and thunderous percussion. Metal emphasizes technical skill, power, and emotional extremity — from melodic power metal to abrasive death metal.

latin.description: A broad category of music from Latin America and Spain including salsa, reggaeton, bossa nova, and cumbia. Latin music is characterized by rhythmic complexity, rich percussion, passionate vocals, and joyful energy.

dance.description: Electronic dance music engineered for clubs and dancefloors. Dance music is defined by a strong four-on-the-floor beat, driving basslines, and euphoric builds toward a drop designed to move a crowd.

alternative.description: A broad category of guitar-based rock music outside the mainstream, characterized by experimental sounds, unconventional structures, and introspective or provocative lyrics. Alternative emerged from post-punk and new wave in the 1980s.

synthwave.description: A genre inspired by 1980s electronic film soundtracks and retro-futurism. Synthwave features lush synthesizer pads, arpeggiated basslines, and a cinematic nostalgic aesthetic evoking neon-lit nights and open highways.

acoustic.description: Music performed primarily on acoustic, non-amplified instruments. Acoustic music emphasizes natural timbre, intimacy, and stripped-down arrangements where the raw sound of the instrument is the focal point.

indie pop.description: A melodic offshoot of indie rock that prioritizes catchy hooks and bright production over guitar distortion. Indie pop blends the artistic independence of indie with accessible, often jangly or synth-driven arrangements.
